data.narrative:
Curio Solutions is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Ed McGinnis and Pete Zweifel that has raised $16M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 peers—3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms spanning seed through Series B stages, including Valar Atomics, Fuse Energy, Helion, and X-Energy.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $16M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical for Series A advancement, yielding $32M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables produced an $808M median valuation, with a range of $200M (Fuse Energy, Series A) to $6.0B (Valar Atomics, Series B). The three-company peer set reflects heterogeneity common in frontier nuclear: Nano Nuclear Energy valued at $808M at Seed stage and Fuse Energy at $200M in Series A.

Triangulated analysis across both methods supports a valuation range of $27M (low) to $929M (high), with a median of $420M. The wide dispersion reflects stage and technology maturity variance within the nuclear sector. Key uncertainties include whether Curio's technical approach and competitive positioning more closely align with earlier-stage (Fuse at $200M) or later-stage (Valar at $6.0B) trajectories, and the degree to which broader nuclear market sentiment will sustain current peer valuations through Curio's next funding event.
